logp.method_description: Solutions of all platinum complexes were made to approximately 100 μM in 0.15 M potassium chloride solution, which minimized aquation of the complexes. These concentrations were later measured in addition to the samples. Aliquots of the stock solutions (2, 3 and 4 mL) were added to 1-octanol saturated with water (4,3 and 2 mL, respectively) so that the total volume of each mixture was 6 mL. The samples were shaken mechanically for 16 h, after which, all samples were allowed to settle for 48 h. Duplicate aliquots were obtained of the water layer from each experiment, and these aliquots were diluted 1 in 100 in 1% analytical grade hydrochloric acid (Choice Analytical). For the 1-octanol layer, 500 μL aliquots were combined with 500 μL 1% analytical grade hydrochloric acid, and subjected to ultrasonication for 10 min. The samples were centrifuged for 1 min, and 1-octanol removed. The Pt content of the remaining water layer was measured. Pt concentrations were measured with a Varian Zeeman atomic absorption spectrometer (240Z AA) equipped with a GTA 120 graphite tube atomizer and a Pt UltrAA hollow cathode lamp (Agilent Technologies) against a standard Pt solution prepared from a 1000 μg/mL Pt stock in 5% hydrochloric acid (Choice Analytical). The lipophilicity, log(P), was calculated as the logarithm of the partition coefficient between water and 1-octanol: log(P) = log10([Pt]_octanol / [Pt]_water)
